children: Arabica coffee futures on ICE closed higher on Wednesday after earlier slumping to a three-month low, while raw sugar and cocoa prices also rose.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled up 3.6 cents, or 1.3%, at $2.759 per lb​​, rebounding from an earlier three-month low of $2.6975.
* Dealers said certified exchange stocks remain very low despite a modest increase in the last few days.

* Stocks stood at 254,480 bags, as of Wednesday, up from a 27-year low of 217,646 bags a week ago. At the same time last year, stocks stood at 643,341 bags. There are only around 18,000 bags pending grading.
* There was also chat in the market about dry weather in Central America, although the outlook for next year's crop in top grower Brazil remains generally favourable.
* Robusta coffee
gained 1.7% to $3,317 a metric ton after slumping to a 3-1/2-month low of $3,218.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
settled up 0.16 cent, or 0.9%, at 17.75 cents per lb, its third consecutive gain.
* Dealers said mills in Centre-South Brazil had focused this season on using cane to produce biofuel ethanol rather than sugar, helping reduce supplies of the sweetener.

* Broker StoneX on Wednesday cut its projected sugar supply surplus for the season ending in September to 1.45 million metric tons from 2.9 million tons, citing delays in the Brazilian harvest and lower sugar content in cane.
* The prospect of lower production in Asian producers such as India and Thailand due to an El Nino weather event has also helped underpin the market.
* White sugar
lost 0.4% to $506.00 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​settled up £130, or 3.3%, at £4,128 per ton.

* Dealers said dry conditions in top producer Ivory Coast had added to concerns about the prospects for 2026/27 production, although a large global surplus in 2025/26 has ensured that short-term supplies remain ample.

* Ghana's cocoa production for the 2025/26 season reached about 771,000 metric tons, beating regulator COCOBOD's initial forecast of 650,000 tons, according to a report reviewed by Reuters on Wednesday.
* New York cocoa
rose 2.3% to $5,528 a ton.
